approach: A straight-line velocity-time graph means constant acceleration; integrating v = u + at over time gives the displacement formula, which is quadratic in time and so traces a parabola.

steps.text: A straight line on the v-t graph means the velocity changes at a constant rate, so v = u + at with a constant.
Displacement is the area under the v-t graph up to time t, which integrates the linear velocity to a quadratic function of time.
A quadratic function of t traces a parabola on the s-t graph, so the Assertion is true and the Reason gives exactly the relation that produces it, making the Reason the correct explanation.
steps.equation: Assertion true, Reason true, Reason explains Assertion

final_answer.value: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is correct explanation of the Assertion.

common_mistakes.text: Doubting that s = ut + ½at² is a true relation for uniformly accelerated motion and marking the Reason false, even though it is the standard equation of motion.
